overview: This Senate resolution recognizes the 1960 University of Missouri Tigers football team, which went undefeated in the regular season, won the Big Eight Conference title, and beat the U.S. Naval Academy in the 1961 Orange Bowl to finish 11-0. It notes the team's strong defense, its coach Dan Devine, and standout players, and supports the team's claim to the 1960 national championship. The resolution honors the players, coaches, staff, students and fans who contributed to the team's success. It is a formal statement of recognition and does not change any law or spending. The Senate approved it on August 6, 2026.
for: Supporters say the resolution gives lasting recognition to one of the most accomplished teams in Missouri's sports history and the people behind it.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and doesn't change any law or spending, and that weighing in on a decades-old college football title is a minor use of the Senate's time.
